newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key 10-yr JGB yield hits record low of 2.060 pct.
newsitem.headline: Key 10-yr JGB yield hits record low of 2.060 pct.

text.p: The yield of the key 182nd 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) fell to 2.060 percent early on Tuesday afternoon, a record low for any benchmark 10-year JGB, traders said.
The bond yield closed at 2.085 percent on Monday.

Traders said scattered buying was detected at the long end of the JGB yield curve from the morning, partly due to comments by Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso, who said reports from the United States earlier this month quoting him as saying it was possible Japan's official discount rate would be raised by the year-end were not entirely correct.
"Aso's comments fit the view, now becoming dominant in the market, that there will be no rate rise by the year-end," said a dealer at an agricultural financial institution.
"But compared with today's rally in JGB futures, the gains in the cash benchmark were limited. That suggested operators are still very cautious about buying at the current high levels," he said.
The previous low for any benchmark 10-year JGB yield was 2.065 percent, recorded last Friday.
